Definition: from G58; relating to the market-place, i.e. forensic (times); by implication, vulgar:--baser sort, low.
BiblicalUsage: Agoraios means 'of the marketplace' — and in Acts it takes two very different shapes. In Thessalonica the Jews took 'certain lewd fellows of the baser sort,' marketplace loafers, and set the city in an uproar against Paul; in Ephesus the townclerk says 'the law is open' — literally, the court days are kept — and there are deputies, so let them accuse one another there.
TheologicalSignificance: Lewd fellows of the baser sort stirred the city against Paul, and this word only says where they lounged — the riot is the story.
